title: Stalks of a sectionwise filtered colimit of presheaves of modules are the filtered colimit of the stalks
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, $\mathcal O$ a presheaf of commutative rings on $X$ and $x\in X$. Let $\mathcal I$ be a small filtered category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and $i\mapsto\mathcal P_i$ a diagram $\mathcal I\to\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O)$ of presheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules on the open subsets of $X$ [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. For every open $U\subseteq X$ let $(\mathcal P(U),(p_{i,U})_i)$ be a colimit of the diagram $i\mapsto\mathcal P_i(U)$ of $\mathcal O(U)$-modules [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and for opens $V\subseteq U$ let $\mathcal P(U)\to\mathcal P(V)$ be the map induced by the restriction maps of the $\mathcal P_i$, so that $\mathcal P$ is a presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules and $p_i=(p_{i,U})_U:\mathcal P_i\to\mathcal P$ are morphisms of presheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules. Let $\mathcal O_x$, $(\mathcal P_i)_x$, $\mathcal P_x$ be the stalks at $x$, with the $\mathcal O_x$-module structures and the $\mathcal O_x$-linear stalk maps $(p_i)_x:(\mathcal P_i)_x\to\mathcal P_x$ of [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Then $(\mathcal P_x,((p_i)_x)_i)$ is a colimit of the diagram $i\mapsto(\mathcal P_i)_x$ in the category of $\mathcal O_x$-modules.

source.place: Sheaves, Section 009D (label section-limits-presheaves, sheaves.tex lines 3367-3398), item (4), lines 3392-3396: $(\colim_i\mathcal F_i)_x=\colim_i\mathcal F_{i,x}$ for presheaves ('The proofs are all easy', line 3398); the same for sheaves is Section 009E (label section-limits-sheaves), item (5), lines 3431-3434; used for modules in Modules, Lemma 01AH (label lemma-limits-colimits, modules.tex lines 204-239), proof of (2)

proof.text: Notation and the cocone. For $a:i\to j$ in $\mathcal I$ write $\mathcal P(a):\mathcal P_i\to\mathcal P_j$ for the transition morphism of presheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules. By [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-modules-colimits-sectionwise], $\mathcal P$ is a presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules and the $p_i$ are morphisms of presheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules; concretely, for opens $W\subseteq U$ and $t\in\mathcal P_i(U)$ one has $p_{i,U}(t)|_W=p_{i,W}(t|_W)$, and $p_{j,U}\circ\mathcal P(a)_U=p_{i,U}$ for every $a:i\to j$ since the $p_{i,U}$ are the coprojections of a colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. By [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] a morphism $\varphi$ of presheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules induces the $\mathcal O_x$-linear map $\varphi_x$, $s_x\mapsto\varphi(s)_x$; this formula gives $(\psi\circ\varphi)_x=\psi_x\circ\varphi_x$ and $(\mathrm{id})_x=\mathrm{id}$, since every element of a stalk is a germ. Hence $i\mapsto(\mathcal P_i)_x$ with the maps $\mathcal P(a)_x$ is a functor from $\mathcal I$ to $\mathcal O_x$-modules, and $(p_j)_x\circ\mathcal P(a)_x=(p_j\circ\mathcal P(a))_x=(p_i)_x$, so $(\mathcal P_x,((p_i)_x)_i)$ is a cocone of $\mathcal O_x$-modules on it.

source.place: Sheaves, Section 009D, item (4) (lines 3392-3398; proof omitted as 'easy', written out here)

proof.text: Every element of $\mathcal P_x$ comes from some $(\mathcal P_i)_x$. By [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] an element of $\mathcal P_x$ is a germ $s_x$ of some $s\in\mathcal P(U)$, $U$ an open neighbourhood of $x$. Since $(\mathcal P(U),(p_{i,U})_i)$ is a colimit of the filtered diagram $i\mapsto\mathcal P_i(U)$ of $\mathcal O(U)$-modules, [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] (1) gives an object $i$ and $t\in\mathcal P_i(U)$ with $s=p_{i,U}(t)$. Then $(p_i)_x(t_x)=p_{i,U}(t)_x=s_x$ by the formula for $(p_i)_x$ of [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk].

source.place: Sheaves, Section 009D, item (4) (lines 3392-3398; proof omitted as 'easy', written out here)

proof.text: Elements identified in $\mathcal P_x$ are identified at a later stage. Let $\sigma,\tau\in(\mathcal P_i)_x$ with $(p_i)_x(\sigma)=(p_i)_x(\tau)$, and put $\rho=\sigma-\tau$, so $(p_i)_x(\rho)=0$ by linearity. By [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] $\rho=t_x$ for some open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ and $t\in\mathcal P_i(U)$, and $p_{i,U}(t)_x=(p_i)_x(t_x)=0=0_x$ ($0\in\mathcal P(U)$ has germ $0$, the germ maps being additive); by the description of equality of germs in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] there is an open $W$ with $x\in W\subseteq U$ and $p_{i,U}(t)|_W=0|_W=0$. By step 1, $p_{i,W}(t|_W)=p_{i,U}(t)|_W=0$. As $(\mathcal P(W),(p_{i,W})_i)$ is a colimit of the filtered diagram $i\mapsto\mathcal P_i(W)$ of $\mathcal O(W)$-modules, [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] (2), case $p_{i,W}(t|_W)=0$, gives a morphism $f:i\to k$ with $\mathcal P(f)_W(t|_W)=0$. Taking germs, $\mathcal P(f)_x(\rho)=\mathcal P(f)_x((t|_W)_x)=(\mathcal P(f)_W(t|_W))_x=0$, where $(t|_W)_x=t_x=\rho$ because $t|_W$ and $t$ agree on $W$. By linearity $\mathcal P(f)_x(\sigma)=\mathcal P(f)_x(\tau)$.

source.place: Sheaves, Section 009D, item (4) (lines 3392-3398; proof omitted as 'easy', written out here)

proof.text: Conclusion. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-criterion] to the ring $R=\mathcal O_x$, the small filtered category $\mathcal I$, the functor $i\mapsto(\mathcal P_i)_x$ of $\mathcal O_x$-modules and the cocone $(\mathcal P_x,((p_i)_x)_i)$ of step 1 (the $(p_i)_x$ are $\mathcal O_x$-linear by [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]): its hypothesis (1) is step 2 and its hypothesis (2) is step 3. Hence $(\mathcal P_x,((p_i)_x)_i)$ is a colimit of $i\mapsto(\mathcal P_i)_x$ in the category of $\mathcal O_x$-modules.
